goal: Test whether the planner reaches the known GO outcome while pruning failed mechanisms, handling mixed evidence, and avoiding incorrect candidate kills.

replay.description: Reveal normalized historical evidence only after the planner selects an experiment.

nodes.name: Clinical Treatment Signal
nodes.question: Does propranolol produce a real IH treatment effect?

nodes.name: Beta-Adrenergic Mechanism
nodes.question: Is beta-adrenergic signaling an important mediator?

nodes.name: Apoptosis Mechanism
nodes.question: Does propranolol depend on inducing apoptosis at relevant concentrations?

nodes.name: VEGF / Anti-Angiogenic Mechanism
nodes.question: Is VEGF suppression a major explanation for the clinical effect?

nodes.name: Beta-Independent Activity
nodes.question: Is there meaningful anti-IH activity independent of strong beta blockade?

nodes.name: SOX18 Mechanism
nodes.question: Does R(+) propranolol interfere with SOX18 function?

nodes.name: Disease-Relevant Cellular Effect
nodes.question: Does at least one viable mechanism alter disease-relevant cell or vascular behavior?

nodes.name: In-Vivo Disease-Relevant Effect
nodes.question: Does the effect reduce disease-relevant vessel formation in vivo?

nodes.name: Pediatric Safety and Tolerability
nodes.question: Is an effective regimen manageable with appropriate restrictions and monitoring?

nodes.name: Clinical Viability
nodes.question: Should propranolol advance for proliferating IH?

experiments.name: HemSC Beta-AR / cAMP / MAPK Functional Assay

historical_result.summary: Published HemSC experiments supported beta-adrenergic involvement through signaling and cell-behavior effects.

experiments.name: Apoptosis / Caspase Assay at Relevant Concentrations

historical_result.summary: At relevant inhibitory concentrations, published studies did not find convincing apoptosis/caspase activation sufficient to explain the anti-IH effect; apoptosis appeared under some higher-concentration conditions.
Historical VEGF/VEGFR findings were mixed and did not consistently track clinical response.

experiments.name: R(+) vs Racemic/S(-) Propranolol Functional Comparison

historical_result.summary: R(+) propranolol retained anti-IH activity in preclinical assays despite much weaker conventional beta-blocking activity.
Preclinical experiments supported interference with SOX18 transcriptional activity and protein interactions.
R(+) propranolol inhibited HemSC endothelial differentiation and vasculogenic behavior in published preclinical work.
Published preclinical in-vivo evidence supported reduced human vessel formation with R(+) propranolol.
Clinical evidence supported an acceptable benefit-risk profile with important contraindications, feeding guidance, monitoring, and known beta-blocker risks.

experiments.name: Randomized Propranolol vs Placebo Efficacy Trial

historical_result.summary: The selected regimen achieved complete or nearly complete resolution in 60% versus 4% with placebo at week 24.

historical_ground_truth.interpretation: Clinical efficacy supports GO, while the mechanistic story is multifactorial: some proposed mechanisms were supported, apoptosis was weakened, and VEGF evidence was mixed.
historical_ground_truth.planner_visibility: Hidden until corresponding evidence is revealed.

dependency_semantics.all: All required dependencies must remain viable.
dependency_semantics.any: At least one alternative route must remain viable.

planner_rules.kill_guardrail: Mechanism-level negatives cannot automatically kill the candidate.
planner_rules.qc_guardrail: Questionable or failed QC cannot trigger candidate kill.

assumptions: Planner outcomes normalize complex published evidence and are not necessarily the wording used in the original papers.
observed_historical denotes corresponding published experimental evidence; composite_historical combines multiple historical findings into one planner-level experiment.
The replay is decision-oriented, not an exact chronological recreation.
Cost/time values are normalized hackathon assumptions.
